#2015. Inside Boreham Wood, the only unbeaten team in England's top seven tiers: Boss LUKE GARRARD explains how play-off heartache and a 'genius' owner are fuelling his swashbuckling side's promotion bid

Published: 21:00 EST, 12 November 2026 | Updated: 17:17 EST, 13 November 2026

Of 252 clubs in the top seven tiers of English football, the last one unbeaten can be found in the pristine confines of Meadow Park, yards from the studios where the Indiana Jones adventures were filmed.

Boreham Wood are on their own crusade. And the Holy Grail is a long-coveted place in the EFL for the runaway leaders of the National League. They have 44 points from 16 games with 44 goals and are 12 points clear ahead of a trip to Yeovil on Saturday, finding success with a distinct passing style.

In a remarkable 4-3 comeback win against Hartlepool earlier this month, Luke Garrard's team made 1,022 passes, beating the Premier League record of 1,015 set by Manchester City against Swansea in April 2018.

The electric start to this campaign is, according to Garrard, fuelled by the lingering pain of defeat in the play-off final at Wembley in May when they conceded an equaliser in the seventh minute of stoppage time and lost on penalties.

'That broke me mentally for four or five days,' the Wood boss tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I reflected hugely and had a long, hard look at myself because I could not walk back for the first day of pre-season without the energy and heart for the job.

'I spoke to the owners and the staff about the first meeting I wanted to have when we came back in. It involved everyone at the club, and it was a message to tell all of them that as much as it hurt us, we needed to use the hurt as our fuel and our driving force.

'We got quite lucky getting some results on the board quite quickly and that builds momentum and belief.'

National League leaders Boreham Wood, under the guidance of their manager Luke Garrard, are the last unbeaten team in the top seven tiers of English football

Boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500. They share Meadow Park with Arsenal Women and Arsenal Under 21s and U18s

Boreham Wood are a slick operation, skilfully run despite crowds seldom breaking 1,500 by chairman Danny Hunter and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director and in charge of recruitment strategy. They are punching above their weight with a mid-table budget.

Hunter senior is a former props master in the film industry who worked at the nearby Elstree Studios among others, and whose father Mickey was a double promotion winning manager of club in the 1970s.

He took control in 1999 and has overseen investment of more than £14million and the rise from the depths of the Isthmian League to the brink of the EFL, forging effective relationships with local authorities and Premier League neighbours Arsenal, who use Meadow Park for their Women, Under-21 and Under-18 teams.

Arsenal ad boards surround an immaculate pitch, and work is underway at the venue on a £4m project to create a covered South Stand terrace incorporating improved 'Fan Zone' style facilities for away fans and a new first-team building.

Garrard's team train in the mornings on the artificial pitches beside the stadium, which are available for community use in the evenings and home in the afternoons to the club's academy.

Manchester City's Iliman Ndiaye and Hull's Sorba Thomas were both nurtured as young players at Boreham Wood. So was Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024 and sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5m in August.

The Abdulmalik fee shattered the non-League record set when Fleetwood Town sold Jamie Vardy to Leicester in 2012.

There was an untidy episode towards the end of the transfer window when Abdulmalik went public to plead for a move, but the Hunters secured an enviable price for their star and in another example of their good housekeeping have yet to reinvest the money in the team. It is still there as a war chest as they target promotion.

Abdul Abdulmalik, a 23-year-old winger signed after his release from Millwall in 2024, was sold to Djurgardens in Sweden for £1.5million in August

The club is run by chairman Danny Hunter (pictured) and his son Charlie, who is the sporting director. Hunter Snr is a former props master in the film industry

The windfall from Wood's famous FA Cup run in 2021-22 was invested into refitting the interiors of the ground including the dressing rooms and swish hospitality areas recognised among the best in non-League.

Meadow Park has a bar bedecked with souvenirs from those games and named in honour of Mark Ricketts, scorer of the goal to beat Bournemouth, who were at the time bound for promotion to the Premier League, and which clinched a date with Everton in the fifth round at Goodison Park.

'At no stage has the chairman given me any pressure to generate money from prize funds and cup runs,' says 41-year-old Garrard. 'It's only ever been about creating moments and memories.

'He (Hunter) is a Boreham Wood boy through and through and it's always been his greatest wish to lead the club into the EFL. He wants to leave a legacy. I adore him, I think he's a genius. We have a great working relationship. I do not take for granted the luxury of being manager here, especially after losing my job two years ago.'

Garrard has a long association with the club. First as a player, briefly in 2005 and then returning for a second spell four years later, a loan move from Wimbledon which became permanent and led him into his first coaching roles and the manager's job.

He took control in 2015 with the Wood in the top tier of non-League for the first time. Three times they reached the play-offs without promotion and there were many highs including Goodison before Garrard's tearful exit after relegation in April 2024, only for him to be back in charge by September.

During five months away, he turned down interest from one club because it took him too far from his family home and received two direct and sobering rejections from National League clubs. Feedback from the first told him he 'wasn't on the list and never would be' and from the second that he 'wasn't good enough' for them.

Perhaps it reveals some of football's inherent petty-mindedness towards Boreham Wood. They are perceived by some as upstarts with limited history and small crowds, putting the noses of 'bigger' clubs out of joint with the streamlined success of their business model and Hunter's backing, like a non-League version of Bournemouth or Brentford.

They have been known to charge scouts for tickets and charge away teams to broadcast, which some refuse to do on a point of principle. For a time, they had a reputation for pragmatic and unattractive football – but not any longer.

Garrard was rejected by two National League clubs and found himself back at Boreham Wood. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it

Prolific striker Matt Rush has is fuelling Boreham Wood's promotion push

Garrard was probably entitled to have expected more interest in his services. Instead, he spent two days following the second of those rejections in earnest conversation with his wife about the need to look for work away from football when out of the blue came a call from Boreham Wood.

Within another two days he was back in his old job. 'The stars aligned,' as he puts it. 'It was the best team in the National South with the best players, the best facilities and the best budget. I had to go and deliver.'

And he did. With promotion back to the National League at the first attempt. Then the near-miss heartache of Wembley. Now this early-season surge thanks in part to the goals of striker Matt Rush. The Wood seem to have emerged stronger despite selling their most talented individual, which is a reassuring situation for any coach.

Unbeaten since April in the National League, they scored 25 goals in seven games in October and League One Wigan became the first team to beat them in any competition this season, in the FA Cup first round on Saturday.

It could yet prove a blessing in Boreham Wood's quest for the Holy Grail.

Now, though, everyone would be glad that the decision was made to sign the young Italian. To say he’s exploded this season would be an understatement and he’s perhaps the biggest gem at the club right now.

“Two or three years ago, we launched Milan Futuro. Our idea was to sign him for that team a year earlier, but we couldn’t reach an agreement with Hellas Verona. They wanted to keep him and decided to send him on loan to Serie B.

“It was winter and we had to hurry. If he had gone to PSV and you had wanted to buy him later, perhaps after playing in the Champions League, the price would have risen to €30 or €40 million. Sometimes you have to speed things up a bit.”

#2007. Man United news: Neville backs Dalot and names three defenders to sell before him

By Axel Clody | 19 Nov 2026 06:43

Diogo Dalot has become one of the targets of Manchester United supporters’ dissatisfaction, but Gary Neville believes the Portuguese full-back is far from being one of the squad’s main problems.

The former Manchester United captain came out in defence of his fellow right-back after the boos Dalot received at Old Trafford and said he would get rid of other players before parting with the number two.

The criticism comes at a time of instability for Manchester United, who are struggling to find consistency in the Premier League and are again facing questions over the individual performances of their players. Dalot was one of the negative protagonists in the draw with Aston Villa, particularly because of the penalty he conceded, and his substitution during the game was greeted with celebrations by the home fans.

‘I would be getting rid of some players before Dalot. Dalot got booed last week at Old Trafford and I was really surprised at that’ - the former full-back said on the ‘Stick to Football’ podcast.

In Neville’s view, Dalot is receiving excessive criticism for frequently playing out of his natural position. The Portuguese is a right-back, but has also been used on the left side, either as a full-back or wing-back, depending on the team’s needs.

The former Manchester United player stressed that this change of role requires adaptation and that Dalot shows a positive attitude in accepting the tasks given to him by the manager.

‘If you put me at left wing-back or left-back, and I am a right-back, and he is too, I would say: “No way, why are you putting me there?”’

The pundit, however, believes Dalot has shown a willingness to help the team, even when he has to play in a position different from the one in which he feels most comfortable.

‘Instead, Dalot literally sticks his hand up and says: “Go on, I’ll play there, I will do anything for the team”. I never see him shirk anything, I never look at him and think he could try harder’ - he added.

Neville’s defence does not mean the full-back is free from criticism of his performances. The Portuguese struggled against Aston Villa and conceded a penalty that contributed to the result. The former captain, however, believes individual performance needs to be analysed within the context of a squad with collective problems and players often shifted out of their usual roles.

Neville also compared Dalot with other members of Manchester United’s defensive unit and said there are players who should be sold before the Portuguese. The former full-back specifically named Noussair Mazraoui, Lisandro Martinez and Matthijs de Ligt.

‘I watch defenders very closely and, if you ask me, I would be getting rid of Mazraoui, well gone, before him, I would be getting rid of Martinez well before him, I would be getting rid of De Ligt gone before him.’

The opinion stands out because the three players named have also faced questions at different points of the season. Mazraoui has been used in different defensive roles, while Martinez has dealt with injury problems and controversy. De Ligt, meanwhile, has also been subject to the team’s fluctuations in performance and changes to the defensive set-up.

Dalot joined Manchester United in 2018 from Porto and has had different spells at the club. After a loan at Milan, he returned to Old Trafford and earned a place in the team, particularly during the 2022-23 season. #2004. Sergio Navarro’s style and the key individuals: Milan Futuro tactical analysis

Milan Futuro decided to go in a new direction this summer by appointing Sergio Navarro, but is it working so far?

Milan launched the Futuro project ahead of the 2024-25 season. with the aim of creating a pathway for academy players to break into the first team. The project was designed to bridge the physical and technical gap between the Primavera and senior football.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Things didn’t go well in year one, as Daniele Bonera didn’t see out the season as the head coach. He recently stated he didn’t think the squad was ready for the level, and ultimately Massimo Oddo was unable to save the team from relegation to Serie D, the fourth tier of Italian football.

With promotion back to Serie C the objective, this summer the Rossoneri turned to Sergio Navarro, a coach with good pedigree in Spain. The Futuro now appear to have a clearer structure, a defined playing identity and the right guidance, as Rohit Rajeev has outlined.

Under Barquero, Milan Futuro operate in a 4-2-3-1 formation. Asanji leads the line, with Ossola playing as the number 10 and Vos and Guernier occupying the wide positions.

Plazotta and Pandolfi form the double pivot, while Cisse and Pagliei partner at centre-back, with Perera and Colombo completing the back four.

Milan Futuro favour a possession-oriented approach, circulating the ball patiently at a measured tempo while waiting for gaps to emerge in the opposition’s defensive structure. They also use passing triangles effectively to create short passing options and play through the opposition’s high press.

In possession, Milan Futuro adopt a 3-1-6 structure, with Barquero showing little hesitation in committing players forward to create numerical overloads in the opposition half.

Asanji positions himself just behind the opposition’s defensive line, keeping the centre-backs occupied and preventing them from stepping forward freely. Meanwhile, Pandolfi and Plazotta maintain parallel positions in the double pivot, providing a stable base for the attacking structure.

In the opposition half, Milan Futuro keep the distances between players very short, allowing them to combine through quick, one-touch passes.

This also helps them create ball-sided overloads, with two or three players surrounding the Milan player in possession to provide close passing options. Once they enter the opposition half, the tempo increases as Milan look to become more direct and progress towards goal.

Similar to Amorim’s approach at Sporting, Milan Futuro form vertical corridors with three players positioned one behind another. This structure facilitates quick passing combinations while also creating movement to manipulate the opposition.

When Milan players drop to form these corridors or create overloads, they often drag defenders with them, opening spaces elsewhere to exploit.

Milan Futuro look to press the opposition high up the pitch, adopting a 4-4-2 shape with a man-oriented pressing scheme. This allows them to put pressure on the opposition’s build-up and restrict the time and space available to play out from the back.

Milan Futuro also set up pressing traps by deliberately leaving the opposition’s wide player unmarked. The pass towards the wide player acts as the pressing trigger, prompting Milan’s players to jump out of their positions and aggressively close down the receiver, while cutting off the available passing options.

Milan Futuro maintain an extremely narrow defensive shape, prioritising the protection of central spaces and forcing the opposition towards the flanks.

Once the opposition attempts to progress through the wide areas, the press shifts across to create numerical overloads around the ball, while Guernier and Colombo provide cover and prevent the opposition from switching play to the opposite flank.

Perhaps the most important aspect of Barquero’s approach is his willingness to build the system around his players’ strengths and allow them the freedom to express themselves.

Rather than focusing solely on tactical adaptability, he appears equally committed to their individual development and helping them grow as footballers. Here are a few examples.

One of Milan Futuro’s methods of chance creation is to play direct passes into Asanji. His ability to position himself between the ball and the opposition defender, using his physicality to shield possession and hold up play, is crucial to this approach.

Rather than asking him to adapt to the role of a more technically oriented, ball-playing striker, Barquero has built a mechanism that makes the most of his existing strengths.

Perhaps the clearest demonstration of Barquero’s coaching ability is his utilisation of Vos and Guernier. Guernier is a natural winger/forward, while Vos is more accustomed to playing as an attacking midfielder.

Within the 3-1-6 structure, Vos often inverts from the left flank into an inside-left role, allowing Perera to provide the width.

At times, he is also given the freedom to interchange positions with Plazotta, allowing him to drop into midfield or advance further up the pitch. This positional freedom helps him develop his midfield qualities and realise his potential.

Guernier, meanwhile, tends to maintain his width, stretching the opposition’s defensive line and creating space for Vos and the other attackers to exploit.

Barquero also gives Guernier the freedom to take on his direct opponent, even when he is outnumbered, allowing him to use his dribbling ability without being restricted by the team’s structure.

Ossola, who is particularly effective at receiving between the lines and turning with the ball, is allowed to operate higher up the pitch, closer to the opposition’s defensive line.

Idrissi, on the other hand, prefers to receive possession deeper, where he can dictate play with his passing range or carry the ball forward through dribbling.

#2001. ‘I probably didn’t realise’ - Sam Winnall reflects on Barnsley FC to Sheffield Wednesday move ahead of derby

Sam Winnall has conceded he “probably didn’t realise” how intense the rivalry between Barnsley and Sheffield Wednesday was when he swapped the Reds for the Owls in 2017.

The now retired 35-year-old was a talismanic figure in his Barnsley days, scoring 48 goals across 155 appearances for the club.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

He was lured away from Oakwell in January 2017, making a controversial move to their South Yorkshire neighbours Wednesday.

The move sparked anger among Barnsley supporters and Winnall received a frosty reception when he faced the Reds as a Wednesday player.

“A lot of what happened was actually well out of my control,” he told The Star. “And I think you look back with not so much regrets from what I can control, but more so just wishing it could have happened at a different time, if I'm going to be totally honest.

“At that time I probably didn't realise how big the rivalry was, being from somebody that didn't come from Yorkshire. There were a lot of things that went on behind closed doors that have never been disclosed.

“It was sloppy in how it was dealt with from all parties and I think there could have been a far more professional way of dealing with it.

“And I look back on it with fond memories, actually, because I think it was a transfer that brought me a few difficulties but I came through it and came out the other side. I grew a level of resilience with what had happened. I don't look back on it with any regrets of how I acted personally.

“People do move between rival clubs. Mine was obviously at a lower level but look at Sol Campbell, Carlos Tevez, it’s football. But I do definitely look back and think it could have been done more professionally.”

Winnall added fuel to the fire when he returned to Oakwell just months after departing, scoring in a 1-1 draw and celebrating in front of the home supporters.

“It's probably been my most asked question since I've retired,” he said. “And do you know what? I look back and if I could have the chance again, I'd do exactly the same.

“That's because it had been quite a difficult time. I'd had quite a lot of stick from different fans and even some former teammates that had spoken about me in the press. I felt a little bit let down by that. I will say this, it was never meant to kind of upset or create any kind of animosity towards any of the Barnsley fans at all.”

Barnsley and Wednesday are set to renew their rivalry in League One tonight (November 20).

#2000. Andy's big night should have been so much more straightforward but that won't matter when he reflects on history made at Hampden

Published: 17:21 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:24 EST, 13 November 2026

If Andy Robertson’s first 101 caps for Scotland taught him anything, it’s that we have never been a nation to make life easy for ourselves. It’s in our DNA.

Why, therefore, would he have expected cap No102 to be any different?

This was meant to have been a celebration of one of Scotland’s greatest-ever servants on the night when he equalled Kenny Dalglish’s total appearances against the whipping boys of Nations League Group B1.

As the cliché goes, there’s no gimmes at this level. But that’s nonsense. This is exactly what Robertson’s special night should have been. A gimme.

The visitors hadn’t registered a goal yet in this campaign, never mind a point. They were rotten when Robertson and Co scored twice without reply in Skopje last month, and it was the same story for much of this forgettable contest.

The problem is that Scotland weren’t much better. In the first half, at least.

Andy Robertson joined Kenny Dalglish on 102 caps as Scotland saw off North Macedonia

Thankfully, they got the job done after the break to ensure it would be a night Robertson will look back on fondly after all.

He’s earned that too, even if his own individual performance didn’t quite hit the heights of so many that have gone before. But nobody will remember that.

Perhaps he knackered himself by covering what must have been around 10km in a small-sided kickabout during the warm-up. He may not have the same turn of pace in his arsenal that he possessed when he first broke into the international fold as a fresh-faced teenager. But, in terms of intensity, the 32-year-old is still an animal, in the nicest possible way. He hassled and harried every one of his team-mates throughout the pre-game stuff, barking out all sorts of instructions along the way.

In many ways, he is still the same standard-bearer he’s always been. It was a shame he couldn’t quite lead the way when the serious stuff got started.

Operating on the left-hand side of a four-man midfield, the Spurs man – as he does as frequently as ever – bombed up and down the flank all night. However, his deliveries from several promising positions weren’t quite up to scratch.

A couple hit the first man. A couple cleared the upright. None caused any sort of alarm in the North Macedonian backline.

Robertson was his customary energetic self as he bombed up and down the left-hand side

He was made to work harder than he would have liked at the other end too, as the visitors threatened to spoil the party on more than one occasion in the second 45.

In truth, he didn’t look particularly comfortable in Sebastien Pocognoli’s new-look side. Then again, few did.

The Belgian will be given plenty of time to really put his stamp on this Scotland team, but there’s no two ways about it. The early signs are uninspiring to say the least.

By the end, people got sick of the attritional style employed by Steve Clarke. Pocognoli arrived with a reputation for going with a more enterprising approach.

Really? It’s fair to say, the wait to see it in action goes on.

It’s not the time to panic. But you get the sense patience is already being stretched amongst some sections of the Tartan Army.

They weren’t shy in airing their frustrations last night. Scott McTominay was on the receiving end of a few grumbles, as was Ben Gannon-Doak who once again did so much right until the all-important crucial last bit.

Yes, he may have won the winning penalty which John McGinn duly slotted away, but let’s be honest, there was more than a touch of good fortune about it.

The Scotland skipper leads his side out at Hampden on a night he will remember forever

He should have burst the net when put clean through by Oli McBurnie long before keeper Stole Dimitrievski caught him near the byline.

The Bournemouth youngster is seen by many as undroppable, and there’s merit to that argument in that Pocognoli doesn’t have anyone else like him to call upon. However, he needs to improve the final part of his game to ensure he becomes Scotland’s main man in the years to come.

Had Scotland been a few goals to the good by the time McGinn stepped up to notch his second of the night, you suspect Robertson may have fancied taking the spot-kick himself.

Still, the record books will show that Robertson’s record-equalling night will ultimately go down as a triumph for all involved, even if it didn’t feel like it at the time.

#1996. ‘Why can’t they?’ - Curtis Davies makes Leeds United claim as Crystal Palace example cited

Leeds have made a strong start to the 2026/27 campaign and sit ninth in the table after 10 games.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Whites boss Daniel Farke has made an effort to quieten talk of a push for Europe, but there are pundits who see qualification as a genuine possibility.

Among them is former Hull City star Davies, who has outlined FA Cup glory as a potential route for Leeds.

He told BOYLE Sports, who offer football odds: “I think you have to dream. It's Leeds United, I'm old enough to know that Leeds are a big club and have obviously got a massive fanbase and I used to watch them play in the Champions League and get to the Champions League semi-finals.

“We're talking about a big football club there. However, recent history hasn't been that. But when you look at the likes of Sunderland after being promoted, getting themselves into Europe, and then Bournemouth, little old Bournemouth, I used to play against Bournemouth in League One.

“It shows that with Leeds United and the stature of that club, why can't they aim for Europe? And especially with the cup competitions, you know, going into the cup competitions trying to do your best in those, you never know.

“I just think when you look at the Crystal Palace model, when you look at the way they got into Europe and the trophy (FA Cup) that they won, it's a good way to do it.”

Leeds defeated Tottenham Hotspur before the international break and have another London giant to slay this weekend, with a trip to Chelsea booked in for tomorrow (November 21).

Xabi Alonso’s Blues will be heavily fancied, but Davies has described them as defensively “fragile”.

He said: “They are one of the most potent attacks probably in English and European football, but defensively they're very fragile.

“I think you're kind of only as good as the whole squad. It's not just about Alonso going in and plugging gaps and being able to teach these defenders how to defend.

“Ultimately it's Chelsea, and the expectancy will always be there to be there or thereabouts at the top. But I think they're kind of whereabouts you maybe expect them to be, I expect them to be in the top four.”

#1993. ‘Only he knows’ - Sheffield United legend opens up on Doncaster Rovers exit and ‘ruthless’ Grant McCann

Billy Sharp has described Doncaster Rovers manager Grant McCann as “ruthless” - but does not hold any grudges regarding his departure.

The 40-year-old left Doncaster at the end of last season, signing off in style with a final-day hat-trick away at Peterborough United.

He later hung up his boots, but did recently come out of retirement to play for AFC Rushden & Diamonds in the FA Cup.

Sharp had expressed interest in a coaching role at Sheffield United while still on Doncaster’s books and believes it had a factor in the decision to release him.

He told the DN4 Podcast: “I don’t hold any grudges at all. He’s a ruthless manager and you’ve got to make decisions. Sometimes you get decisions wrong. I’m sure it did have a part to play, I think so, but only he knows.

“I think you have to be ruthless as a manager. I’m stubborn as well. If I ask myself, if I was manager and a player came to me... but I don’t know. It was different because I was coming to the end of my career, I’m a Sheffield United fan, I was trying to think about the future.

“It wasn’t that I wasn’t enjoying training or playing. It had been arranged to retire. But I don’t know, I really wanted the opportunity. I thought it was a great opportunity for me to be in the game for the next 15, 20, whatever years.”

Sharp has repeatedly expressed a desire to move into coaching and with his playing days now seemingly behind him, the iconic marksman can shift his focus.

Given the wealth of experience possessed by the Sheffield United legend and ex-Leeds United man, he would arguably be a shrewd addition to an array of coaching set-ups.

“Grant always said to me about doing a bit of coaching at Donny,” he said. “He obviously brought Greeny (Paul Green) up.

“When I was injured, towards the back end of the season, looking out of that physio room, wanting to be on that training pitch, I could see myself doing a bit of coaching as well.”

#1991. GdS: Worth the price tag – how Moreira became ‘untouchable’ for Milan and Belgium

It has been a positive international break for Diego Moreira, who continued his excellent form from club football.

As La Gazzetta dello Sport write this morning, Ruben Amorim will welcome Moreira back to Milanello soon. The winger has become a regular starter and producing goals and assists, but the Portuguese coach knows the pitfalls of the match against Frosinone all too well.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Therefore, starting Thursday – when the squad will be fully back together after the day off tomorrow – everyone’s minds will be focused solely on the new busy schedule awaiting the Rossoneri until Christmas. More specifically, seven matches from Sunday until December 19th.

Immediately after the last international break, the Rossoneri drew away to Sassuolo, a result that certainly wasn’t greeted with a smile. The goal is to avoid repeating that misstep against Alvini’s team, and Moreira will be key to that.

Despite his 22 years of age and the €50m valuation plus bonuses that could have weighed heavily on his shoulders, Diego hasn’t taken long to win over Milan fans. In his last six league matches (he missed two due to injury), he’s scored four goals and provided three assists.

He has also demonstrated his ability to switch roles with ease, playing as a winger on the right or left, as a wing-back or even as a full-back. He plays with the boldness of someone who targets his opponent and tries to dribble past him, something that fans always appreciate.

Moreira always seeks one-on-one situations, both due to his strengths and the explicit request of Amorim, who asks his wide players to create numerical superiority. Diego is succeeding remarkably, as his assist for Christian Pulisic in the derby shows, as he got past Carlo Augusto and crossed.

Moreira made the difference against Italy on Sunday too: not only did he score the fourth goal, which he celebrated by making a gesture of ‘one, two, three and four’ with his fingers, but he also kept accelerating, hit the woodwork, shot wide once more and had two shots blocked by his opponents.

He set up De Bruyne for a shot, had more touches than anyone else in the opponents’ area (11) and often took on Calafiori and Dimarco, delighting the crowd with a spectacular backheel. He had around 50 touches and 27/31 completed passes, earning the applause of the entire stadium when he came off.

Moreira is currently captivating thanks to his drive and desire. He’s that way at Milan and he’s that way with the national team. That’s why there’s a version of the Rossoneri with him and another without him which, frankly, isn’t as threatening.

Amorim carefully integrated him into the team’s operations at the start of the season, but now he has broken the padlock off and now considers him a key player in the team. This doesn’t mean he won’t need a breather, given the schedule, but the coach will have to think about the right moments to rest.

With four goals in Serie A (one every 121 minutes), he’s already matched his four goals from last season in Ligue 1, and he has no intention of stopping. He feels the confidence in himself and the team.

The leap from Ligue 1 to Serie A didn’t bother him. In fact, he intends to continue dancing on the pitch, just like in the derby or against Italy. On Sunday, he wants to show he has the same energy with which he brought Italy to its knees. Milan and San Siro await him.

#1990. ‘Wasted’ – Paul Ince questions £50m Man Utd transfer decision

Paul Ince still cannot wrap his head around Manchester United’s decision to spend £50million on Andrey Santos in the summer transfer window.

Santos completed a £50m move from Chelsea over the summer, arriving alongside Youri Tielemans and Carlos Baleba as the Red Devils sought to bolster their depth in central midfield.

Santos enjoyed an encouraging pre-season, but started only four of United’s first ten Premier League matches under Michael Carrick before his sacking.

Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival may represent a fresh start for the £50m midfielder, but Ince believes United would have been better served spending that money elsewhere over the summer.

‘Why did they spend £50m on Santos?’ Ince told The Sun. ‘That’s £50m wasted. They could have put that into the defence or bought a striker.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘They have [Kobbie] Mainoo, who needs to develop. He needs to be playing, not Santos.

‘Tielemans, again, fantastic at Villa but it’s a different conversation when you come to United.

‘Baleba didn’t play a lot last year. He comes in for £70m, plays a couple of games and he’s injured again.

‘The game’s changing. It’s not all pass, pass, pass now. You’ve got to win your duels. You used to hear Pep Guardiola say every time, “We didn’t win our duels, we didn’t win our tackles”.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The game’s more physical, more powerful.’

United are expected to provide Pochettino with backing to strengthen his squad in the January transfer window.

But Ince fears that his former club will struggle to attract the world’s best talents given their current predicament.

‘What you’ve got is players playing for Manchester United, not Manchester United players,’ he added. ‘That’s a big difference.

‘Who’s a Manchester United player out there? [Declan] Rice, Jude Bellingham. They are who you should be going for.

‘Since Sir Alex Ferguson left it’s been a complete disaster. Would every player in the world want to come to United? They don’t, because it’s a basket case there, a shambles.’

#1989. Man Utd transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino puts prolific 19-goal Spurs target on January 'wishlist'

By Lewis Blain | 19 Nov 2026 07:21

Manchester United are preparing to strengthen their attack in the January transfer window, with new boss Mauricio Pochettino already keen to add more firepower.

The Argentine is understood to have put four main centre-forward targets on his winter 'wishlist', including a prolific striker also attracting interest from former club and top-flight rivals Tottenham Hotspur.

Benfica talisman Vangelis Pavlidis has emerged as a particularly exciting possibility after an outstanding start to the season in Portugal.

The Red Devils are ready to spend significantly to back Pochettino in January, with Benfica striker Pavlidis among the names under consideration, according to reports.

Spurs and Barcelona have also been linked with the Greece international, who is said to be open to a move to the Premier League in 2027.

One source revealed: "Pochettino is eager to make sure United have more of a goal threat. He's already been discussing names, and Vangelis Pavlidis is someone who fits the bill."

Pavlidis is not the only striker on United's radar, with Galatasaray's Victor Osimhen also admired by Pochettino. However, a deal for the Nigerian is considered less realistic due to his substantial transfer fee and wage demands.

Former Brentford forward Ivan Toney is another option, while Borussia Dortmund's Serhou Guirassy is being monitored as a potential rotation option, too.

Pavlidis has scored 19 goals in 19 appearances across all competitions this season, while also providing four assists. His remarkable return means he has found the net once every 72 minutes on average.

The 27-year-old's immense goalscoring numbers make him an attractive proposition for United, particularly with Benjamin Sesko having struggled with injuries.

His current form suggests he could provide an immediate improvement to Pochettino's attacking options, offering a reliable source of goals during the second half of the campaign.

Importantly, Pavlidis' age does not necessarily have to come at the expense of Sesko's long-term development, with the Slovenian still viewed as part of United's future once fully fit.

Osimhen may be the more ambitious acquisition, but Pavlidis appears to offer a potentially more attainable solution without sacrificing significant attacking quality.

If United are serious about challenging at the top end of the Premier League, adding a striker with 19 goals already this season could be a major step forward.

#1987. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#1986. Kevin De Bruyne to leave Napoli 'the sooner the better', his wife announces: Man City legend, 35, desperate to quit his 'not nice existence' after rows with team-mates, bosses and fan issues

Published: 17:01 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 17:58 EST, 13 November 2026

Kevin De Bruyne's wife Michelle has opened up on her family's struggles in Naples and desire to move back home to Belgium one day.

De Bruyne, 35, joined Napoli in the summer of 2025 after leaving Manchester City following a legendary ten-year spell.

But things haven't gone to plan in Italy, with De Bruyne struggling for fitness in his first season, while he also clashed with former boss Antonio Conte.

The situation hasn't improved much this time around under Max Allegri as Napoli currently sit 10th in Serie A, and reports broke earlier this season that the Belgian midfielder was involved in a dressing room bust-up with team-mates.

And De Bruyne's wife Michele, who he married in 2017, reflected on the turbulence in an interview with Belgian magazine NINA back in September.

'Of course, we think about the future together,' he said. 'And increasingly often, we say to each other: "We are going to live here in Limburg. The sooner we get here, the better".'

Kevin De Bruyne's wife Michelle has opened up on her family's struggles living in Naples

De Bruyne moved to Napoli in the summer of 2025 after a glittering 10 years at Manchester City

Limburg is a province in Belgium, and although Michelle insisted that she thought Naples was a beautiful place to live with great weather and food, she spoke about the toll that life in Italy has had on her partner and their three children, Mason, Rome and Suri.

'Kevin leads a very restricted life in Napoli,' she added. 'It's not much fun for him. Besides, we can't do anything together as a family in the city. That's the other side of the coin, isn't it?

'In Manchester, it was different. Where we lived, people had seen us so often that it wasn’t special anymore. We could walk out the door there without a single photo being taken. In Naples, that is impossible.'

She later added: 'At a certain point, football is no longer the priority. You have achieved everything, done everything. Why would you then turn your children’s lives upside down?'

De Bruyne, who is one of the highest paid players in Italy, signed a two-year contract when he arrived at Napoli but it wasn't certain that he would make it into the second part of that deal in the summer.

Reflecting on his first year ahead of the World Cup, De Bruyne insisted he was 'happy' that Conte had departed.

'Obviously it was difficult for me because Conte has a very different vision of football to mine,' De Bruyne said.

'In truth, I never had the opportunity to play in my preferred position. In any case, I always tried to give my all for the team. We played very defensively. If you try to win every game by a one-goal margin with a 4-5-1 formation, you play a certain type of football.

De Bruyne signed a two-year deal at Napoli and is unlikely to extend his time in Italy

'At the start of the season, we sat back even deeper. Our centre-forward scored just 10 goals, so you know the statistics are not going to be great…'

He later added: 'For me, yes (I'm happy Conte has gone). As far as I am concerned, he was not obliged to stay. There were promises made last summer on the way that we would be playing, but at the end of the day not much of it happened.

'I found that a pity. Football needs to be enjoyable, and unfortunately, I found that aspect lacking.

'There’s no point beating around the bush, we have different visions of football. I never got to play in my position under Conte.'

#1984. Chelsea transfer news: Blues learn new asking price for in-demand forward amid Man City interest

By Lewis Blain | 19 Nov 2026 07:39

Chelsea are facing growing competition for Club Brugge forward Nicolo Tresoldi, with Premier League rivals Manchester City among the clubs monitoring his situation.

The 23-year-old has attracted considerable attention after an impressive goalscoring campaign in Belgium, with several European sides now considering a move.

However, the asking price for the Germany-born striker has risen amid increasing interest, potentially complicating the Blues' pursuit.

Tresoldi has scored 14 goals in all competitions for Club Brugge this season, including five in the Champions League, with his hat-trick against Inter Milan a particular highlight.

North London duo Arsenal and Tottenham Hotspur have also been linked with the forward, while Serie A giants Juventus and AC Milan are closely monitoring his availability.

According to reports in Italy (via Sport Witness), Milan are currently considered the leading contenders, with Tresoldi's support for the Rossoneri potentially helping their pursuit.

However, Chelsea and City remain in the picture, although their chances of securing his signature could be complicated by Club Brugge's increasing demands.

Tresoldi was initially valued at more than €50m (£42m), but it is now believed that the Belgian outfit wants €60m (£50m) as they look to capitalise on the growing interest.

Milan are keen on a January move, with the player's preference for a switch to San Siro potentially giving them an advantage. Ultimately, though, their ability to meet Brugge's asking price could determine whether a deal is possible.

Although Tresoldi's performances make him an attractive target, Chelsea's chances of landing the forward appear rather complicated.

His preference for AC Milan is an obvious obstacle, particularly with the Italian club already keen to explore a January transfer.

There is also the question of where he would fit into Xabi Alonso's plans, with Joao Pedro currently Chelsea's first-choice centre-forward. City face a similar dilemma, given Erling Haaland's established position in their attack.

For Tresoldi, regular football should be an important factor in deciding his next move, particularly at this stage of his development.

Chelsea may therefore be better served exploring alternative forward options rather than committing significant resources to a player who could favour a move elsewhere and face competition for minutes at Stamford Bridge.

#1983. Di Marzio: Endrick and Tresoldi deals ‘not a financial issue’ for Milan – the situation

AC Milan have the financial capability to go out and sign their top targets in January, according to Gianluca Di Marzio.

Several reports and even the words of owner Gerry Cardinale have made it very clear that Milan plan to be busy in the winter mercato. The main target seems to be a forward to complete the attack, as well as a centre-back to help out the defensive department too.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Among the names linked have been Real Madrid’s Endrick, Club Brugge’s Nicolo Tresoldi and Sporting CP’s Goncalo Inacio. It’s one thing having the list of names, but it is another having the money and the possibility of doing a deal mid-season with the selling club.

During last night’s segment on Sky, Gianluca Di Marzio (via MilanNews) was asked whether Milan can realistically pursue names like Endrick and Tresoldi, who are likely to cost over €50m each.

“That they has the strength to do these kinds of deals, yes. They demonstrated it over the summer, so I don’t think there’s a financial issue,” he began.

“Whether they manage to sign one of the two… Endrick, as far as we know, José Mourinho hasn’t changed his mind and therefore doesn’t intend to part with him in January. But Endrick is a Cardinale obsession, just as he was a Roma obsession during the summer.

“We’ll have to see if Mourinho changes his mind in the month and a half before the transfer window opens. He hasn’t changed his mind at the moment, so I see the situation as complicated at the moment.

“Just as it’s complicated for Brugge to sell Tresoldi. Brugge are a club that doesn’t need to sell and always sells at least one key player in the summer, precisely to try to get to the end of the season with its players.

“Milan are looking for a striker, looking for a back-up for Ramos. The figures I’ve read, 60-70 million, are very, very high figures to try to convince Brugge to sell him. It’s a deal that – given the player’s objective value – I think is around 50 million. In my opinion.

“But Brugge are unlikely to sell him in January. Above all, Milan is looking for a striker to be a back-up for Ramos; it’s not like Ramos and Tresoldi will play together. In the sense that Milan has always played with a centre-forward.

“Above all, they need to provide this center forward with plenty of playable balls rather than buy another. Because if Ramos doesn’t receive balls in the penalty area, he struggles to score, and Tresoldi struggles to score either.

“They need a striker to get Camarda playing. I think Camarda will go and play and therefore an investment will be needed in a player who can be a suitable deputy for Ramos.”

#1982. Barcelona respond as Alejandro Balde pushes for Man Utd transfer

Barcelona have confirmed they have no plans to sell Alejandro Balde and insist the Manchester United-linked left-back remains an ‘important player’ for the club going forward.

Balde has been with Barca since the age of just eight, making a total of 173 appearances in all competitions since breaking into the first-team squad back in 2021.

In that time, the 23-year-old has helped the Catalan giants win seven pieces of silverware, including three La Liga titles – the most recent coming under Hansi Flick last season.

However, Balde has become an increasingly peripheral figure at the Camp Nou in recent months, with all five of his appearances this term coming from the substitutes bench.

Balde currently finds himself behind both Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart in the pecking order at Barca and the Spain international’s career appears to be at a crossroads.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

According to Spanish publication Mundo Deportivo, this has forced Balde to consider his options and the full-back is understood to be keen on joining Mauricio Pochettino’s Manchester United in January.

Other reports suggest that ‘everything Balde has heard about his situation has come through press conferences’ and the defender views the Premier League as a possible escape route.

The subject of Balde’s future has proven a major talking point both in the media and amongst Barcelona’s fanbase – and the topic was raised during Catalunya Radio’s joint interview with club chiefs Bojan and Deco on Wednesday.

Asked about the possible sale of Balde this winter, football coordinator Bojan replied: ‘Balde is a fantastic lad.

‘Obviously, he’s in an uncomfortable situation. The player wants to play.

‘He’s one of our own and he’s still an important player. It’s true that he’s not playing right now, although he’s ready if the manager needs him.’

Deco, Barca’s sporting director, was similarly unequivocal when asked if a transfer deal could be on the cards for Balde.

‘No,’ the ex-Barca, Chelsea and Portugal responded.

‘There is also the player’s side, but he hasn’t told us anything about being unhappy, that’s not the case.’

Manchester United had been actively looking to strengthen at left-back in the summer in order to provide support and competition for Luke Shaw, the club’s only specialist in the position other than academy product Harry Amass.

The Red Devils ultimately failed to bolster their full-back options, though, which has come back to bite them already this season, with Shaw sidelined for the last month through injury.

Diogo Dalot was therefore forced to fill in as a makeshift left-back in the bleak final weeks of Michael Carrick’s tenure at the Theatre of Dreams.

It’s understood Lewis Hall had been identified as United’s number one left-back target ahead of the 2026/27 campaign, but Newcastle made it clear the England international would not be sold for anything other than an astronomical price.

Hall would go on to put pen to paper on a new long-term deal at St James’ Park, tying him to the Magpies until 2031.

Bournemouth’s Adrien Truffert, Fulham’s Antonee Robinson, RB Leipzig’s David Raum and Crystal Palace’s Tyrick Mitchell have also been linked in recent months.

#1981. NEC vs PSV Eindhoven - prediction, team news, lineups

By Adepoju Marvellous | 19 Nov 2026 08:04, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 20:42

The 2026-27 Eredivisie season resumes with NEC welcoming PSV Eindhoven to Stadion de Goffert on Saturday evening, as both teams kick off matchday 13.

Both sides recorded impressive victories in their final outings before the November hiatus and will be aiming to build on that momentum.

With Feyenoord and Ajax dropping points against Heerenveen and FC Twente earlier in the day, PSV travelled to the Kooi Stadium to face Cambuur with the opportunity to move top of the Eredivisie table - a chance they seized emphatically with a 5-2 triumph.

That was a much-needed response from Peter Bosz’s men, who had suffered a 2-1 defeat to Club Brugge in the Champions League just four days earlier.

Playing before their title rivals gives De Rood-witten the chance to open up a four-point gap at the summit with a victory this weekend. However, away matches at NEC have been challenging recently, with the last four yielding just one win and 12 goals conceded.

PSV’s trip to Nijmegen is further complicated by a daunting assignment against Real Madrid next Tuesday, leaving Bosz with a delicate balancing act, especially after an international break in which several players were involved.

With a league-high six goals scored in the opening 15 minutes this season, Saturday’s visitors have an opportunity to exploit a notable weakness in NEC, who have conceded first in six of their last eight matches and in eight of the last 10 meetings between the sides.

After a difficult start to the season, NEC appear to be getting back on track, as a 3-2 victory over FC Utrecht on November 8 secured back-to-back wins for the first time since August and made three victories from their last five outings (D1, L1).

While confidence appears to be returning, Dick Schreuder’s side have yet to solve their defensive issues, conceding in 19 consecutive matches across all competitions; their last shutout came in the season opener against Olympiacos.

Having failed to keep a clean sheet in 20 consecutive meetings with PSV, the Eniesee know they will need to deliver in attack to stand any chance of success and have shown they can, scoring at least three goals in five of the last six encounters against this weekend’s opponents.

Saturday’s hosts also face a looming European assignment, giving Schreuder additional selection considerations as he seeks a third consecutive win over his opposite number in 2026, following two victories in March just 11 days apart.

Scott has established himself as one of the most sought-after central midfielders in English football having joined Bournemouth from Bristol City back in 2023.

With attentions beginning to turn towards the January transfer window, speculation is mounting that the 23-year-old could have his head turned amid strong interest from the Premier League’s elite.

Up until this point, Bournemouth have publicly played down speculation that Scott could be on the move, especially midway through the campaign when they risk derailing the side’s encouraging progress under Marco Rose.

However, it’s understood an offer in region of £100million could be enough to convince the Cherries into selling Scott in what would undoubtedly be one of this January’s biggest deals.

During a wide-ranging interview on the Rio Ferdinand Presents YouTube channel, Lampard made it clear just how highly he rated Scott when he was asked to name his dream Premier League midfield three on current form.

‘I don’t want to leave anyone out because there are some teams that are doing some stuff… I’m loving what Brighton are doing at the moment but you do come back to the bigger players sometimes, maybe Cole Palmer or Rayan Cherki,’ the Coventry head coach told Ferdinand.

‘I love Alex Scott at Bournemouth, I think he’s quality.

‘He’s injured now for a short period but I think he’s real quality in that modern all-rounder [role], in the double six/eight.’

Revealing other candidates for his midfield three, Lampard added: ‘I’ve got to put Elliot Anderson in there, in my opinion, for the way he’s playing.

‘I’m trying to think of the attacking options… I think I’d put Anderson and Declan Rice as the two sixes and then I’ll go for an eight/ten.

Lampard went on to express his admiration for Martin Odegaard, explaining how he had shut down one of his close friends who had been criticising the Arsenal captain.

‘I think he’s a really good player and it’s just a common thing that comes with the territory.

‘It’s fine and Declan will just shrug it off.’

#1976. Wes Brown: ‘Man Utd still have every chance of Champions League qualification’

Wes Brown believes Manchester United should still be aiming for a top-five finish this season after Mauricio Pochettino was appointed head coach.

The former Tottenham and Chelsea boss has officially taken the reins at Old Trafford after his final two matches with the United States national team.

Pochettino has undoubtedly been thrown in at the deep end, with United winless in their last eight Premier League matches and facing Liverpool in his first game on Sunday.

But former Red Devils defender Brown believes that the Argentine has the quality to inspire a quick turnaround from his new crop of players.

‘Poch is very experienced, and he has his own style of play, but it’s all about consistency, he told Metro. ‘Making the players believe they’re good enough and making sure they do it week in, week out.

Read exclusive analysis of the biggest stories in football with Metro's weekly football newsletter In The Mixer. Sign up now for free.

‘We’ve had no momentum; we’ve played well here and there in games, and when we did we managed to score, but at the same time we’ve been very poor at times and open to teams scoring at will, making loads of mistakes.

‘The confidence isn’t there, but he’ll be coming in and just trying to get consistency through the team.

‘When a new manager comes in, the players really make an effort, that’s just the way it goes, but then it’s up to the manager to keep that going through the season, and whether or not he’ll be able to, we’ll all have to see.’

Pochettino brings with him extensive experience in the Premier League but also a proven track record of nurturing young talent into the first team.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

And Brown is hopeful that academy duo Shea Lacey and Harry Amass could benefit from the Argentine’s arrival, adding: ‘If anyone, you think those two might come in and get a game under the new manager to show what they can do.

‘I think at the moment, you are looking at Shea Lacey and thinking, “Yeah, he can get a game”. He delivers, he runs, he works hard.

Pochettino faces a trip to Anfield for his first game in charge (Picture: Getty)

‘But I also think when you’re in a position where you don’t necessarily just bring in the young lads as well. I think that’s a tough gig if I’m being honest, and you can’t just bring them in when the team’s like this.’

Pochettino will have to endure a frenetic start to life in the United dugout, with a run of eight games in 21 days starting at Anfield on Sunday.

But with plenty of the season still ahead, Brown thinks United should still be aiming high if they can start fast under their eighth permanent boss since Alex Ferguson’s retirement.

‘There’s still a chance of getting into Europe, 100 per cent,’ Brown added.

‘Even though it’s been very disappointing, even if you look at the table now, the gap is not that big. It’s maybe 8-9 points from a European place, if that.

‘So you’ve still got to have that in the back of your mind. It’s Manchester United; that’s where you aim to be, if not higher, and I’m sure Poch will definitely be looking to get us in that sort of area and going in that direction.’

Brown was speaking to Metro ahead of the year’s second Counter-Strike Major.

#1975. Arsenal star Max Dowman smashes Jude Bellingham's record - but a less-familiar name should catch Thomas Tuchel's eye ahead of Euro 2028: THINGS WE LEARNED from England U21's defeat to Portugal

Published: 16:46 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 18:41 EST, 13 November 2026

Max Dowman smashed Jude Bellingham's record on an icy cold night in Bristol to become the youngest player to ever play for England's Under-21s.

The 16-year-old was sent on with 30 minutes to go by Lee Carsley in a move that energised an Ashton Gate crowd that went home frustrated after a 1-0 defeat inflicted by Afonso Moreira's first half goal.

But this was to be Dowman's night, smashing the previous record set by Bellingham when he made his England Under-21 debut against Kosovo in 2020 aged 17 years, two months and six days old. Dowman does not turn 17 until December 31.

Under-21s boss Lee Carsley has been keen long before this international break to try to shield Dowman from the weight of expectation.

But on he came, replacing the lively Amario Cozier-Duberry with a smile on his face and a quiet confidence that he didn't take long to show off, bursting past two Portuguese markers before four huddled together to gang up on him.

Breaking records is nothing new to a player that already holds one for being the Premier League's youngest-ever goalscorer, thanks to his goal against Everton last season.

Max Dowman wrote his name into the record books once more, playing for England Under-21s

Dowman came on to rich applause on a cold night in Bristol to shatter Jude Bellingham's record

The Arsenal teenager was lively playing off the right as he now targets the 2027 U21 Euros

Dowman is both the youngest player to ever win the Premier League and his outing in the Champions League against Slavia Prague last season saw the then-15-year-old become the youngest-ever player to appear in that competition.

By the time next summer's European Championships, which England will attempt to win for a third successive time, rolls around, rising star Dowman could well have earned the right to be this team's main man.

'We've only got three games left before the Euros [next summer],' Carsley explained.

'So it's important that he puts himself in the shop window to be on the plane.

'It's important that he keeps playing well, getting minutes, showing a really good attitude, like he has done.

'I thought he was outstanding when he came on tonight. I thought all of the subs made a real impact.

'I thought Max was unlucky not to get an assist... he made a great pass to Mikey Moore.

'He took up some really good positions, both in the 10 and out wide, he's got a big future ahead.'

His immense talent was one reason why Arsenal sent Ethan Nwaneri, who Dowman played alongside for part of his cameo, to Marseille on loan, and then similarly to Borussia Dortmund, eager not to block the 16-year-old's pathway.

Carsley knows the diamond he has on his hands and will want to take great care in helping polish a player that this crowd, this England team and this management group know has genuine world class potential.

Speaking of Nwaneri, this felt like a big camp for him. A big camp in the sense that he's falling down the pecking order at Dortmund and is back with a manager that has been so vital in his development.

Nwaneri was part of that 2025 group that won the Euros in front of Thomas Tuchel and he'll have seen the likes of Elliot Anderson and Alex Scott kick on to get to the seniors.

As previously mentioned, Nwaneri was moved out of the way by Arsenal to aid Dowman's development, not an easy pill for a player as talented as he is to stomach when his own development journey is at such a critical juncture given he is, to the surprise of many, still only 19.

'I think we have to remember his age as well,' Carsley added when asked about Nwaneri by Daily Mail Sport.

'He's very young is Ethan and he's another one that we've got a lot of hope for. He's got a lot of potential.'

Ethan Nwaneri was pushed to the side at Arsenal to benefit Dowman but England is different

Lee Carsley has been a crucial figure in the development of Nwaneri and this camp was timely

It was telling that even when Dowman came on, even with the groundswell of excitement at his introduction, it was Carsley's call to keep Nwaneri in his preferred No 10 position with Dowman slotting in on the right.

Nwaneri has only started four games on loan at Dortmund this season and has not managed a single start in the Champions League.

His close control, his quick burst over five yards and the fluidity of his movement was a timely reminder that yes, Dowman is the rising star everyone came out to see, but Nwaneri won't get pushed to the side again without a fight.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is a name not all will be familiar with but come next summer, with the Euros in his sights and promotion to the Premier League on the agenda with Middlesbrough, that could all be about to change.

The 21-year-old has had to be very patient, waiting until last month to make his debut at this level after years of finding himself overlooked.

Here, in what was just his third Under-21 appearance, he showed over the course of 61 minutes why the days of being looked past should be over.

One of the big frustrations in the FA right now at Under-21 level is the lack of touchline wingers. Rio Ngumoha, still only 18, has never been capped at the level and has instead been catapulted into the first team, while many, like Ethan Nwaneri, prefer playing inside.

'The more we can get our wide players one v one the better,' Carsley said. 'I think sometimes we leave them isolated and the opposition are able to double up on them.

Amario Cozier-Duberry is not a household name at international level but his talent is immense

'It's important that our game plan can't just be to get the ball wide and hope for the best.'

Dowman, on in place of Cozier-Duberry is a 10, rather than a right winger which is where he came on, and so a player like Cozier-Duberry, who is on loan at Middlesbrough from Brighton & Hove Albion, is worth his weight in gold.

Here in Bristol he was routinely drawing two defenders and at times three; Portugal knew full well how a quick flip-flap of the ball, or one clipped pass over the top, was enough for the Englishman to take the top off the back-line.

His loan at Bolton Wanderers last season complicated an international journey that has seen him play at Under-16, Under-17, Under-18, Under-19 and Under-20 level, but that's all in the past.

England need a genuine, pacy threat out wide if they are to win a third straight Euros. Cozier-Duberry showed here exactly why he should be it.
